name: scry
description: Session-start checks for codebase architecture, running stack, repository health, concurrent activity, machine pressure, and untrusted Markdown. Requires every dispatch to a model to choose that model rather than inherit a default silently — subagents, workflow agents, and metered agent CLIs invoked through Bash — warns on first contact with a large and actively-worked source file, and guards expensive Elixir force-rebuilds.

interface.shortDescription: See repository and machine state at session start
interface.longDescription: Adds session-start context about codebase architecture, the stack the system actually runs on, repository hygiene, concurrent Claude and Codex activity, local machine pressure, and why every repository Markdown file is untrusted historical material. Also installs one PreToolUse hook that DENIES a first attempt at an artifact-discarding Elixir rebuild (`mix compile --force`, `rm -rf _build`) and states its cost; running the command again within five minutes passes through untouched. Set SCRY_BUILD_GUARD=0 to disable that hook. A second PreToolUse hook DENIES any dispatch that names no model, because a blank model is not a default -- it silently inherits whatever default is already in place, for the whole run, multiplied across a fan-out. That covers Agent and Workflow dispatch, and metered agent CLIs run through Bash, where an unflagged call falls back to the CLI's own config default; SCRY_METERED_CLIS (default codex) sets which CLIs are covered and SCRY_METERED_CLI_GUARD=0 switches that part off. No model is forbidden; only the absent choice is. A PostToolUse note reports what a premium model draws after it is deliberately chosen, and SCRY_PREMIUM_MODELS sets which models draw it. A further PostToolUse advisory speaks on first contact with a source file that is both large and actively worked, naming what it did not return and what goes wrong silently at that size.
defaultPrompt: Use Scry to check the state of this workspace.
